metadata.title: Cooper Kupp goes for 50 yards in loss
metadata.description: Cooper Kupp caught five of ten targets for 50 yards in the Seahawks' 17-14 loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Kupp had arguably his best game of the season, with season-highs in targets, receptions, and yards, lacking only a touchdown. He is a bit of a risky start most weeks, as his volume has been low for the most part. A near 20% target share this week is a nice sign of life, but we will need to see more consistency to really feel comfortable starting him.

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp - Season-high 10 targets vs. Denver
metadata.description: Kupp caught five of 10 targets for 50 yards during the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Kupp accumulated 15 targets through the first five games of the regular season, but the veteran wide receiver was peppered Thursday by Sam Darnold on Thursday, who attempted a season-high 51 passes. It was the first time since Week 12 of the 2024 season (with the Rams) that Kupp saw double-digit targets, and he finished second in that category Thursday behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (16). Kupp's best days are behind him, but he's a valuable safety blanket for Darnold in the passing game. Kupp will bring a 16-179-1 receiving line (25 targets) into Seattle's Week 7 bout against the Chiefs on Sunday, Oct. 25.

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp - Only two catches vs. San Francisco
metadata.description: Kupp caught two of three passes for 15 yards during Sunday's 32-29 loss to the 49ers.
metadata.analysis: It was the fourth time in five games this season that Kupp saw three targets or fewer, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba pacing the Seahawks' pass catchers with a 5-102-1 receiving line on eight targets during Sunday's loss. There's no expectation that Kupp will recapture the form he had during his tenure with the Rams, and he figures to be limited to a complementary role in the Seahawks' offense. That said, Smith-Njigba has popped up on each of Seattle's first two estimated practice reports as a limited participant due to an ankle injury. That is worth monitoring ahead of Thursday night's road game against the Broncos, whose defense will likely be without star outside cornerback Pat Surtain (ankle).

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp part of crazy ending Sunday
metadata.description: Cooper Kupp caught 2-of-3 targets for 15 yards in the Seahawks 32-29 loss against the 49ers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: On 4th-and-10 with the game on the line, Kupp caught an 8-yard pass, made one defender miss and dove for the first down. After review, he wound up being short by one yard. He remains off the fantasy radar.

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp Remains an Unreliable Fantasy Option
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Cooper Kupp continues to trend in the wrong direction rather quickly. Kupp went from being the WR1 in 2021 to fighting for targets and a roster spot over the last couple of years, especially after leaving the Rams for the Seahawks. This year, Kupp has mustered just nine catches for 114 yards and a touchdown, and last week, he was held to a measly one catch for 13 yards. Last Sunday marked the third time this season he has produced six or fewer fantasy points in PPR leagues. He is clearly overshadowed by Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the passing game, but he also found himself behind AJ Barner and Rashid Shaheed in the pecking order more often than not this year. After all, those young players are trending up while he's trending down. Kupp can be benched or left on waivers in all leagues ahead of Week 5 against the 49ers, who have limited opposing receivers to the sixth-fewest fantasy points this year.

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp - One catch in Week 4 win
metadata.description: Kupp caught one of two targets for 13 yards in Sunday's 30-23 win over the Chargers.
metadata.analysis: Kupp played 34 of 60 offensive snaps and ran 17 routes on Sam Darnold's 26 dropbacks. The veteran wide receiver has failed to reach 50 receiving yards in any of the first four games, totaling nine grabs for 114 yards and a touchdown on 12 targets. He's well off the fantasy radar with Jaxon Smith-Njigba dominating the looks in Seattle.

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp quiet Sunday
metadata.description: Cooper Kupp caught 1-of-2 targets for 13 yards in the Seahawks 30-23 win over the Chargers.
metadata.analysis: Kupp remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp Could See Limited Involvement in Week 4
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Cooper Kupp is not a viable fantasy option in Week 4 against the Los Angeles Chargers. Kupp enters this matchup as the WR50. He has only received 11 targets through three games. Kupp put up solid fantasy numbers in Week 3 due to a late touchdown reception. However, Week 4 does not project to be as competitive a matchup. Seattle is -7 on Sunday, and Kupp does not tend to receive much volume in games in which Seattle dominates. This passing offense runs through wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Given JSN's 39% target share, there is very little to go around for the rest of the wide receivers in this offense. You can leave Kupp on your bench or on waivers in Week 4. He is untrustworthy for fantasy despite his important role in the Seahawks' success.

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp - Late touchdown in high-scoring battle
metadata.description: Kupp caught four of five targets for 46 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 33-31 loss to the Commanders.
metadata.analysis: Kupp was able to take advantage of the return of quarterback Sam Darnold in Week 3, connecting with Darnold for a seven-yard score with 2:55 left in the fourth quarter. The wide receiver doubled his season total in targets Sunday, and he has now caught eight of 10 targets for 101 yards and a touchdown over three games so far in his second season with Seattle.

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp finds end zone in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: Cooper Kupp caught four of his five targets for 46 yards and one touchdown in the Seahawks' 33-31 Week 3 loss to the Washington Commanders.
metadata.analysis: Kupp took advantage of increased involvement in the Seattle passing attack, recording more than two receptions for the first time in three contests Sunday. The wideout remains difficult to trust in all formats ahead of a Week 4 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers.

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp Hard to Trust Despite Favorable Week 3 Matchup
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Cooper Kupp gets a favorable matchup with Washington in Week 3, but his role has been too small to trust in most fantasy lineups. Kupp has four catches for 55 yards on only five targets through two games, including two receptions for 20 yards against Arizona last week. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has dominated the passing game, while Rashid Shaheed drew six targets in Week 2 alone. Sam Darnold is back after missing last week with a glute injury, and Kupp does not carry a game designation despite dealing with a back issue during practice. Washington has allowed 482 passing yards and seven passing touchdowns through two games, so the matchup gives Seattle plenty to work with. Kupp just has not been seeing enough of that opportunity himself. He sits at WR74 in RotoBaller's latest Week 3 rankings. The matchup gives him some deep-league appeal, but five targets in two games makes Kupp difficult to use as anything more than a desperation flex.

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp (back) available to play Sunday
metadata.description: Cooper Kupp (back) is available to play in Sunday's game against the Washington Commanders.
metadata.analysis: Kupp is going to play on Sunday. He was dealing with a back injury earlier in the week, but it's nothing serious at this point and won't affect his availability against the Commanders. He isn't expected to be a good fantasy option in this matchup, however, even with Sam Darnold (glute) set to make his return for the Seahawks.

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp - Limited Wednesday

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp is Limited on Wednesday
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Cooper Kupp (back) was a limited participant during Wednesday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. Kupp was dealing with a back issue last week as well, but he still managed to suit up on Sunday. He hauled in both his targets for 20 yards in the win over the Arizona Cardinals. The expectation is that the Seahawks are just being careful with the veteran wideout to begin the week. Barring any setbacks, Kupp should be ready to go for the Week 3 matchup against the Washington Commanders. Kupp has four receptions for 55 yards through the first two games of the season. He offers some deep league appeal, but he isn't someone who must be started right now.

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp - Gains 20 receiving yards Week 2
metadata.description: Kupp caught both of his targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 31-7 victory versus Arizona.
metadata.analysis: Kupp wasn't very productive, but that was the case for all of Seattle's wideouts aside from Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who dominated with nine catches for 155 yards and one touchdown. The only other Seahawks player to log more than Kupp's two targets was Rashid Shaheed, who put up a 3-35-0 line on six targets. Through two weeks, Kupp has tallied a modest four receptions for 55 yards. With Smith-Njigba dominating the targets in Seattle's passing game, Kupp may struggle to put up consistent production this season.

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp snags two passes in win
metadata.description: Cooper Kupp caught both of his targets for 20 yards in the Seahawks' 31-7 win over the Cardinals.
metadata.analysis: Kupp was third on the team in yards and targets, but that didn't amount to much. He's best left on the bench or on waivers.

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp Looking to Stay Involved in Seattle's Offense in Week 2
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Cooper Kupp (back) logged a limited practice session on Wednesday with a back issue, but was a full participant on Thursday and Friday and enters a Week 2 matchup with the Arizona Cardinals without an injury designation. He will look to stay involved in the offense against the Cardinals after seeing three targets and recording two receptions for 35 yards in a Week 1 victory over the Patriots. Kupp's 35 yards ranked second on the team behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (122), while he was tied for second on the team in both targets and receptions. Kupp played 39 snaps, which was the second-most for Seattle's wide receivers behind Smith-Njigba (45). With starting quarterback Sam Darnold out, Kupp will need to build a connection with Drew Lock, who will start while Darnold is inactive. Kupp is projected to score 5.8 points (half-PPR) this week, but is off the radar and currently ranks as RotoBaller's No. 75 wideout for Week 2. It is not necessary to have Kupp in your lineup, but his situation is worth paying attention to moving forward.

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp - Good to go for Week 2

metadata.title: Cooper Kupp Upgraded to Full Practice Participation on Thursday
metadata.description: Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Cooper Kupp (back) was a full participant in practice on Thursday, per Josh Weinfuss of ESPN. Kupp was limited in practice on Wednesday with a back injury, but it appears he is trending toward being good to go for his team's Week 2 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. The 33-year-old recorded two catches for 35 yards on three targets in Seattle's Week 1 win over the New England Patriots. Kupp was on the field for 78% of the Seahawks' offensive snaps against New England, second most among Seattle receivers behind only Jaxon Smith-Njigba. However, Kupp averaged just 4.4 targets per game while playing the WR2 role in Seattle in 2025 and will now be catching passes from backup quarterback Drew Lock for at least one week. Assuming he's able to play in Week 2, Kupp profiles as a deep-league flex option at best for fantasy managers.
